external_prior.source: Palmer Antarctica LTER 2011-12 Annual Report; historical hypothesis attributed there to Fraser and Patterson 1997
external_prior.role: externally specified threshold; no threshold search in mina

primary.predictor: log1p number of colony-code groups with >50 breeding pairs at census year t
primary.baseline: island fixed effects + current log1p abundance + secular year

fixed_sensitivity.predictor: fraction of island breeding pairs residing in >50-pair groups

synthesis_with_colony_network.effective_colony_number_result: supported with positive coefficient and positive held-out-year gain
synthesis_with_colony_network.active_colony_count_result: positive coefficient but negative held-out-year gain
synthesis_with_colony_network.external_large_group_count_result: positive held-out-year gain but negative coefficient
synthesis_with_colony_network.interpretation: The supported colony-topology signal is not equivalent to retaining more >50-pair groups. The data favor a distribution/evenness property of breeders among subcolonies over the pre-existing directional large-group-retention hypothesis.

supported: The externally fixed >50-pair variables contain held-out-year predictive information beyond island identity, current abundance and secular time trend.
Both large-group count and the fraction of breeders in large groups reduce leave-one-year-out prediction error.
Their fitted coefficients are negative rather than the externally predicted positive direction.
not_supported: the historical directional hypothesis that retaining more >50-pair breeding groups predicts better next-year island growth after current abundance and time trend are controlled
a threshold-search interpretation; 50 pairs was fixed externally and no alternative thresholds were examined
a causal claim that large breeding groups reduce demographic resilience
equivalence between the >50-pair result and the supported effective-colony-number result
ecological_interpretation: Large-group status and colony-network diversity are not interchangeable. Conditional on current island abundance and year, a more even distribution of breeders among colonies predicts slightly better next-year performance, whereas having more or a larger fraction of >50-pair groups predicts in the opposite direction to the historical hypothesis despite improving prediction. This points away from a simple 'large groups are protective' mechanism and toward colony configuration/evenness as the more relevant internal state.
next_gate: Do not search alternative pair thresholds. Seek external spatial/topographic information for colony codes, or consolidate the multi-scale ecological manuscript before opening another mechanism family.
